title: I Had (Past Tense) A Dream
subtitle: White privilege sucks for white people, too. An MLK Day meditation.
body_html:
I am an Italian-American, but that rounds up to White, and I get all the privilege that comes with whiteness. White privilege, however, is a vampire turd. Here's what you get when you accept white privilege into your heart: nothing. White privilege serves itself. All of us who benefit from white privilege do so blithely, at a price that would’ve made Faust blush.

I will do my best to explain. When I get pulled over by the police, I'm white. It doesn't matter if the cop is black or if the cop is white. I am a white guy driving a car when it comes to the police pulling me over.

I don't have to be afraid of driving my car through any neighborhood in America when it comes to the cops. When I go to Greenwich, Connecticut, which is just swarming with police officers, I get to drive around and think, oh, thank God, this is a safe neighborhood. Look at all the law-enforcement officers here to keep the riff-raff out. Thank goodness, it is such a safe community.

If you're black, however, your relationship with that same drive in that same community is different. It's a stressful experience. It's frightening. And even if you're cool with it, imagine you have a kid. Let's imagine your kid has a psychiatric illness. Let’s imagine your kid is driving a car while having a psychiatric illness. Let's imagine that psychiatric illness could lead to erratic behavior. And now, with a deep breath, let's imagine your non-white child gets pulled over by the police while psychiatrically unwell and acting erratically.

And now, in keeping with the standards of journalism in this newsletter, I present some data. Black males are more likely to die from police violence1:

Between the years of 2010 and 2014, Black males aged 10 years and older were nearly three times more likely to die as a result of police violence than their White counterparts (Buehler, 2017).

It has not gotten better since then, as you can guess. Additionally, if you have a mental illness, the data demonstrates the risk of death in an encounter with the police goes up:

In this study, using all civilian deaths (N = 1099) in the U.S. in 2015, compiled independently by The Washington Post and The Guardian newspapers, we identified characteristics of each interaction between the police and the deceased, such as whether the decedent was armed. We expanded the database to include systemic factors possibly related to these deaths, and examined death rates by demographics, presence of mental illness, and state-level predictors. Twenty-three percent (251 of 1099) of individuals killed during interactions with police in 2015 displayed signs of a mental illness. Race (African-American [RR = 2.57] compared to non-Hispanic Whites [95% CI 2.08–3.18]) and presence of mental illness (RR = 7.16 compared to no mental illness, 95% CI 6.21–8.25) were strongly associated with such fatalities. Individuals with mental illness were more likely to be armed with a knife (OR = 3.1, 95% CI 2.1–4.6), and were more likely to have been killed at home (OR = 2.8, 95% CI 1.9–4.0). … Our finding that many persons with mental illness were killed at home and were not brandishing a firearm suggests that more effective de-escalation methods might reduce the incidence of fatal outcomes.2

Emphasis added by your author. White privilege is also sane privilege. It is privilege that extends to those who can hold their sh*t together. Some people are not afraid of being murdered at baseline.

White privilege is terrific—until it's not. Like for example, you can be white all day, every day; you can be as white as the president-elect. And then, one of your kids falls in love—and has a child—with somebody who is black. And then, suddenly your grandchild? They can end up black, too. What matters in a mental health crisis when the cops pull you over on the side of the road?

Well, it's if you can hold your sh*t together while not being black. Compare “being black” and “brandishing a knife at the police,” and you will see, statistically, they are equally bad plans. If you put black and mentally ill together, you are around 1,000% more likely to die than if you are white and able to stay calm, with no mental illness driving your behavior in the wrong direction.

White privilege extends only as far as it makes internal sense for white privilege to extend. White privilege is more than willing to eat its own young. White privilege exists to protect only itself. Not you, your kids, or your grandkids, even if they're sick and haven't done anything wrong. The police culture in America was forged, in part, to maintain the system of slavery. This wasn't created by anyone alive today, but it doesn't matter— it's baked into the DNA of policing in America. Our country has endless guns, and we've decided that mass shootings, literally every single day, even at schools all across the country, are better than anybody anywhere having to think twice about whether they should lock and load. And we have police officers, who, by the way, are victims of this process as well. Many of them get PTSD from the same shootings that kill the black, brown, and mentally ill people that they're shooting to death3. Yes, there's an 800% higher rate of PTSD in officers who are involved on the shooter side of a police shooting.4

I’m not blaming the police. Our officers and firefighters are victims of this system, as well. Their lives, their minds, and their inner peace are routinely destroyed. It sacrificed on the altar to the very same privilege that encourages them, implicitly and explicitly, not to take any risks and to pull their gun and shoot that black kid straight in the heart. Please don’t risk your family, your pension, or your life—not for some kid who isn’t yours, officer. Here is a podcast I made with a military veteran friend about this very problem:

This isn't true in other countries. Japan has almost no fatal shootings. In China, there's a mass stabbing every once in a while, and nearly everybody survives. We've made remarkable choices in the service of white privilege. It means guns for everybody, and it means dead children; it's the leading cause of death of children in America.

This means that nobody is comfortable when they call 911 for help. If they're unwell in a way that unsettles a police officer? One of the “safest choices” that an officer can make is to shoot that mentally ill person dead. That's not an option if all you have on you is a Billy Club, as in the UK.

We created a police force capable of using lethal force at a whim to preserve the institution of slavery. That same system exists to this day. It utilizes deadly force on people who are not white and people who are mentally ill, with overwhelmingly higher rates than they do with white males.

White males are not protected by this system. White males also die more in shootings because there are more guns and more gun violence than there are anywhere else in the world that isn't a war zone. Our treatments are crummy5, by the way. Oh, and what about war zones?

It's safer to be deployed with the US military overseas to an actual active war zone like Iraq or Afghanistan6 than it is to grow up as a black kid in Baltimore.

It's safer to be deployed by the US military overseas to a war zone like Iraq or Afghanistan in the global war on terror than it is to get home, have your gun in your own home, and end up shooting yourself with it.7 Suicide, not active duty deployment to a war zone, is a leading cause of death for our military service members.8

We had the guns to keep the slaves in line. Even when slavery is gone, the vestigial guns perpetuate the system. White privilege is, of course, much more than this one problem with policing. This vast and systemic inequity would take more than just one essay to address.

White privilege kills white people. White privilege kills black and brown people. White privilege kills mentally ill people. White privilege sustains itself with the guns it's made endlessly available. White privilege will, eventually, turn on you, like a viper, the second you try to get in its way. Never forget that white privilege is not your friend. Its whole job, all day, every day, is to convince you it's a friend of every white person and every person of color. Just get in line, stop complaining, and do not make a fuss. White privilege serves white privilege. It doesn’t care what nightmares you have.

On this inauguration day, it's worth remembering the villain isn't any one of us; it's the system we all implicitly agreed should continue. We never had a conversation about whether it should continue; instead, we had thousands of discussions, millions, and the outcome of every one of those conversations was: shut up, don’t make a fuss.

Martin Luther King had a dream, and it will take longer to realize it. White privilege was and is a viper, and it will sting you dead rather than betray itself; it is a snake eating its own tail. In the Reverend MLK’s memory, I say:

We will all be judged by the content of our character; the question is only when. Let us hold each other accountable on earth rather than face judgment day never having done so.

Share

1

Smith Lee, J. R., & Robinson, M. A. (2019). “That’s my number one fear in life. It’s the police”: Examining young Black men’s exposures to trauma and loss resulting from police violence and police killings. Journal of Black Psychology, 45(3), 143-184.

2

Saleh, A. Z., Appelbaum, P. S., Liu, X., Stroup, T. S., & Wall, M. (2018). Deaths of people with mental illness during interactions with law enforcement. International journal of law and psychiatry, 58, 110-116.

3

Gersons, B. P. (1989). Patterns of PTSD among police officers following shooting incidents: A two-dimensional model and treatment implications. Journal of Traumatic stress, 2, 247-257.

4

Hartley, T. A., Sarkisian, K., Violanti, J. M., Andrew, M. E., & Burchfiel, C. M. (2013). PTSD symptoms among police officers: associations with frequency, recency, and types of traumatic events. International journal of emergency mental health, 15(4), 241.

5

Prior installments include Ambien, Prozac, Xanax, Klonopin, Lurasidone, Olanzapine, Zulranolone, Benzos, Caffeine, Semeglutide, Lamotrigine, Cocaine, Xylazine, Lithium, dextromethorphan/bupropion and Adderall, Gabapentin, and others.

6

Bird, S. M., & Fairweather, C. B. (2007). Military fatality rates (by cause) in Afghanistan and Iraq: a measure of hostilities. International journal of epidemiology, 36(4), 841-846.

7

Pruitt, L. D., Smolenski, D. J., Bush, N. E., Tucker, J., Issa, F., Hoyt, T. V., & Reger, M. A. (2019). Suicide in the military: Understanding rates and risk factors across the United States’ Armed Forces. Military Medicine, 184(Supplement_1), 432-437.

8

Anestis, M. D., & Bryan, C. J. (2013). Means and capacity for suicidal behavior: A comparison of the ratio of suicide attempts and deaths by suicide in the US military and general population. Journal of affective disorders, 148(1), 42-47.
